newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan China-concept shares up on Hong Kong surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan China-concept shares up on Hong Kong surge.

text.p: Taiwan's China-concept shares surged at mid-morning on Monday on the back of gains in China-related shares in the Hong Kong stock market ahead of the British colony's handover on July 1, brokers said.
China-concept shares are companies with invesmtment or investment plans in China.

After 60 minutes, or at 0200 GMT, tyre maker Cheng Shin Rubber rose T$2.3 or 5.11 percent at T$47.3 and bicycle maker Giant surged T$2.7 or 6.01 percent to T$47.6, while the overall index was up 0.09 percent.

"These China-concept shares, especially those that already have several years of operations in the mainland, have started to enjoy profit returns and are expected to perform even better in the future," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.

Yang said several securities newspapers at the weekend had given wide coverage of China-related shares' strong performance in Hong Kong, and many analysts expected Taiwan's China-concept shares to follow suit.
